subject: Cloud Computing
title: Search Engines in the Cloud
description: A fast breakdown of Search Engines in the Cloud for builders.

hook.text: Your e-commerce site has 10 million products. A user types 'red sneakers size 10.' Full-text search finds it instantly.

buildup.text: Search engines like Elasticsearch and OpenSearch index data for fast text queries, filtering, and ranking.

discovery.text: Cloud-managed versions — Amazon OpenSearch, Elastic Cloud — handle clustering, scaling, and backups for you.

twist.text: Search clusters are resource-hungry. They consume heavy memory and CPU, making them one of the costlier cloud services.

climax.text: Good search feels invisible. Bad search makes users leave. It's one of the most impactful features to get right.

punchline.text: Great search feels like magic. It's actually an expensive engine.

quiz.question: Why are cloud search engines considered expensive?
options: They consume significant memory and CPU for indexing and querying
Cloud providers charge per search query executed
Search engines require dedicated physical servers

details.summary: Cloud search engines like Elasticsearch, OpenSearch, and Algolia provide full-text search, filtering, and analytics on large datasets with millisecond response times. Managed services handle cluster scaling, patching, and backup for these operationally complex systems.
details.whyItMatters: Search is a core feature of most applications. Managed search services make powerful full-text search accessible without the significant operational burden of running search clusters yourself.
takeaways: Full-text search with relevance ranking and faceted filtering
Elasticsearch and OpenSearch dominate cloud search deployments
Managed services reduce the heavy operational burden

faq.question: What is the difference between Elasticsearch and OpenSearch?
faq.answer: OpenSearch is an open-source fork of Elasticsearch created by AWS after Elastic changed its license. They are functionally similar for most use cases. Elasticsearch is maintained by Elastic with commercial features, while OpenSearch has AWS-backed community development.

faq.question: When should you use a search engine vs a database?
faq.answer: Use search engines for full-text search, fuzzy matching, relevance-ranked results, and log analytics. Use databases for transactional operations, exact lookups, and relational queries. Many applications use both: a database as the source of truth and a search engine for queries.
